articles.headline: Seahawks-Broncos on TNF Week 6: Highlights, TDs, key plays
articles.description: Follow all the biggest plays and highlights from Thursday night's game between Seattle and Denver.
articles.headlineJa: TNF第6週 シーホークス対ブロンコス：ハイライト、TD、キープレー
articles.descriptionJa: シアトル対デンバーの木曜夜の試合から、すべての主要プレーとハイライトをお届けします。
articles.body:
DENVER -- The Broncos (3-2) are hosting the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (3-2) on "Thursday Night Football" (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video).

Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle's slow start to the 2026 season is part of a bigger malaise for Denver's offense. The Broncos are 31st in the league in plays of 20 or more yards (with 11). Waddle is 65th in the league at 11.3 yards per catch and 69th in receiving yards per route run at 1.63, far below his 2.27 yards per route run last season with the Miami Dolphins. It's those types of figures that pushed coach Sean Payton to retake playcalling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb after four games.

Seattle coordinator Brian Fleury's offense ranks eighth in scoring at 26.8 points per game. But it's also 25th in expected points added and 26th in ESPN's efficiency metric, indicative of flaws that Seattle's defense and special teams have helped cover. The Seahawks do lead the league in takaeaways with 11 and points off turnovers at 44.

Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Broncos reporter Jeff Legwold will bring you all the highlights and key plays from Thursday night, so be sure to check back in once the game kicks off.

articles.headline: NFL Week 6 uniforms: Broncos, Seahawks throw it back in TNF matchup
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 6, led by throwbacks from the Broncos and Seahawks.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週のユニフォーム：ブロンコスとシーホークスがTNFの対戦でレトロスタイルを披露
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスとシーホークスのレトロユニフォームを筆頭に、NFL各チームの第6週の着用ユニフォームを紹介します。
articles.body:
Throwback Thursday is coming to the NFL in Week 6 with a matchup for nostalgic eyes on "Thursday Night Football." The Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks will each wear their throwback uniforms in the game.

Denver's look is a callback to the 1977 uniforms that honor the "Orange Crush" era. The orange jerseys include oversized white numbers in legacy blue trim, while white pants and legacy blue helmet complete the look. Featured on the lid is the iconic hissing Bronco and "D" on the side. The Broncos boast a 5-0 record since debuting the combination in the 2024 campaign.

Seattle is throwing it back to the 1990s with its royal blue jerseys, and matching silver helmet and pants. Running on the uniform's sleeve is a classic Seahawks logo on top of green and blue stripes. Neatly, the old Kingdome appears on the inside collar. The matte silver helmet is similar to what the franchise wore in its early history. The Seahawks have a 4-3 record in the throwbacks since debuting them in 2023. 

The alternate uniform space is well represented, too, as the New Orleans Saints are wearing their all-white color rush uniforms with a white helmet against the New York Giants. New Orleans unveiled the white lids in 2025 with a new tri-color stripe down the center and a black face mask for the first time in franchise history. A mini fleur-de-lis is subtly included on the tri-color stripe.

articles.headline: Jon Morris, former AFL and NFL center with Patriots, dies at 84
articles.description: Jon Morris, who played 11 of his 15-year AFL and NFL career with the Boston and New England Patriots, has died at age 84.
articles.headlineJa: 元パトリオッツのAFL・NFLセンター、ジョン・モリス氏が84歳で死去
articles.descriptionJa: AFLおよびNFLでの15年間のキャリアのうち11年間をボストンおよびニューイングランド・パトリオッツで過ごしたジョン・モリス氏が、84歳で亡くなりました。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Jon Morris, who played 11 of his 15-year AFL and NFL career with the Boston and New England Patriots, has died. He was 84.

Morris' death was announced Thursday by the Patriots. The cause of death was not disclosed.

A six-time AFL All-Star center for the Boston Patriots from 1964 to 1969, Morris was also a Pro Bowl selection in 1970, when the team joined the NFL as part of the AFL-NFL merger.

A standout at Holy Cross, Morris was selected by the Boston Patriots in the fourth round of the 1964 AFL draft and by the Green Bay Packers in the second round of the NFL draft. He opted to remain in New England, beginning a professional career that would last 15 seasons, including three with Detroit from 1974 to 1977, and his final season with Chicago in 1978.

"Jon Morris was one of the great players who helped build the foundation of our franchise," Patriots chairman and CEO Robert Kraft said in a statement. "For generations of Patriots fans, he represented the toughness, dedication and pride of those early teams."

Morris helped anchor an offensive line during his tenure that included future Patriots Hall of Famers Gino Cappelletti, Babe Parilli and Jim Nance.

Morris' honors earned him induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame in 2011. He was also included on the Patriots' 50th anniversary team in 2009.

articles.headline: Panthers to visit an Eagles team that was already reeling before losing Hurts to a blood clot
articles.description: — The Carolina Panthers had already been installed as road betting favorites as they prepare to visit Philadelphia and face a banged-up Eagles team riding a three-game losing streak.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズ、ハーツが血栓により離脱する前から苦境に立たされていたイーグルスを訪問へ
articles.descriptionJa: カロライナ・パンサーズは、3連敗中で怪我人が続出しているイーグルスとのフィラデルフィア遠征を前に、アウェイながらブックメーカーの優勢と見なされています。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — The Carolina Panthers had already been installed as road betting favorites as they prepare to visit Philadelphia and face a banged-up Eagles team riding a three-game losing streak.


              Then came a shocker: Eagles quarterback and former Super Bowl MVP Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game because of a blood clot in his calf.


              Tanner McKee, a fourth-year backup with two career starts, is now tasked with trying to salvage a season that has already turned into an injury-riddled disaster.


              The Eagles can only hope that running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith can return from injuries that sidelined them during losses that sunk morale among Philly fans just two seasons removed from a Super Bowl championship.


              “You’ll never get me making any excuse for anything,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. “Our job is to find ways to win regardless and that’s what we’re working on doing. That what we’re trying to do. Obviously, at this point, we’ve lost more than we’ve won, so we haven’t done a good enough job.”


              The 26-year-old McKee's only starts have come in Week 18 in each of the past two seasons, when the Eagles had clinched playoff berths and decided to rest Hurts. He has completed 54 of 88 passes for 597 yards with five touchdowns and one interception.


              That almost sounds like a single-game stat line for Carolina's Bryce Young. He's on pace to throw for 5,389 yards and 38 touchdowns, which would shatter franchise records.


              “A guy whose career started off, I would say slow, watching it from afar and with time has become a good, solid quarterback,” Sirianni said of Young.


              The Eagles would surely settle for a good, solid performance from McKee.


              The Panthers, at least publicly, have downplayed the idea that their game plan just became a bit less complicated in trying to shut down McKee rather than a dangerous dual threat in Hurts.


              “Since I have been in the league they have been to two Super Bowls and won one, so this is a team that knows how to win,” Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd said.


              The defending NFC South champion Panthers (2-2) are coming off an early bye and lead their division.


              Some Carolina players might have wanted to test themselves against Hurts. The rest will surely take what should be a nice edge, and the oddsmakers agree. The Panthers moved from 1 1/2-point favorites to 3 1/2-point favorites after Hurts' medical issue was revealed Thursday.


              “I wish he wasn’t out,” Panthers linebacker Jaelan Phillips said. “I like competing against great players. And Tanner is a great player, too, but I was excited to play against Jalen.”


              Need to know
              Carolina (2-2) at Philadelphia (2-3).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS.


              Latest odds: Panthers b

articles.headline: Sean McVay faces former offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur for first time when Rams host Cardinals
articles.description: — The game between the Rams and Cardinals on Sunday is about more than the latest matchup pitting Sean McVay against one of his former offensive assistants — in this instance,
articles.headlineJa: ラムズ対カージナルス戦、ショーン・マクヴェイが元オフェンシブ・コーディネーターのマイク・ラフルーと初対決
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日のラムズ対カージナルスの試合は、ショーン・マクヴェイがかつてのオフェンス・アシスタントの一人と対峙するという、単なる最新の対戦以上の意味を持っています。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — The game between the Rams and Cardinals on Sunday is about more than the latest matchup pitting Sean McVay against one of his former offensive assistants — in this instance, Arizona’s first-year coach, Mike LaFleur.


              The Rams (2-3) are trying to get on track after an erratic start to the season, while the Cardinals (1-4) are seeking to recapture the success of their surprising season-opening visit to SoFi Stadium, when they knocked off the building’s other tenant, the Chargers. In short, there is a lot more for both sides to worry about rather than friendships and returning to one’s former place of employment.


              “As much as I love Sean, I haven’t really thought of him too much,” LaFleur said. “I’m sure he’s kind of feeling the same way about me right now.”


              McVay downplayed the familiarity LaFleur has with Los Angeles’ systems and personnel after spending the previous three seasons as the Rams’ offensive coordinator. Asked if he has to be cognizant about using certain tactical tools such as snap counts or hand signals this week, McVay cautioned there are limits to those considerations.


              “There’s, like, everybody around the league is (somebody) that’s been in this building before now, so we try to be mindful of it,” McVay said. “You’re aware of a couple things, but I think you want to be careful to chase a ghost because it is still a player’s game.”


              Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford agreed with that line of thinking, even while taking into account LaFleur’s contributions to his MVP season last year.


              “I think he’s a fantastic coach, you know, have a great relationship with him, and I know that he knows a lot of what we do,” Stafford said. “We still got to go out there and execute it. You know, we got to go out there and play. They got to go out and execute their game plan this week.


              “Obviously, with only one year removed, there’s things you sit there and you could stay up all night and go, ‘Oh, does he think this or think that?’ You just go play the game.”


              And even if LaFleur does have the knowledge to shut down the most productive offense in football — the Rams are averaging 424.4 yards per game — whether he has the personnel to make it happen is a different matter. The Cardinals have allowed at least 31 points in every outing during their four-game losing streak and rank last in the NFL in scoring defense (32.4 points).


              “I love Mike, and it’s about the Rams versus the Cardinals, and we’re going to try to get after him as good as we can this week,” McVay said.


              Need to know
              Arizona (1-4) at Los Angeles Rams (2-3).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:05 p.m. EDT, Fox.


              Latest odds: Rams by 12 1/2.


              Against the spread: Cardinals 2-3; Rams 2-3.


              Last week: Cardinals lost to the Lions 45-21; Rams los

articles.headline: Patriots on upset alert as Geno Smith brings a no-INT streak into Jets matchup with Patriots
articles.description: — The New England Patriots are coming off their best performance of the season, doing almost everything they wanted during a 28-point win over the...
articles.headlineJa: ジェノ・スミスがインターセプトなしの記録を携えてジェッツとの対戦へ、パトリオッツは番狂わせを狙える状態に
articles.descriptionJa: ニューイングランド・パトリオッツは、今シーズン最高のパフォーマンスを見せ、28点差での勝利の中で望んでいたプレーのほぼすべてを実現させた直後です。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- — The New England Patriots are coming off their best performance of the season, doing almost everything they wanted during a 28-point win over the Las Vegas Raiders. 


              But there's plenty of reasons for New England to be on guard against the Jets this week. And it starts with Geno Smith. 


              It's not just that the veteran New York quarterback has not thrown an interception this season in five starts, the longest opening stretch to a season in his career without one. He also has had the Patriots number of late, having won in his past two trips to Foxborough (with Seattle in 2024 and Las Vegas in 2025).


              Last season's win with the Raiders included Smith completing 70% of his passes for 362 yards while spoiling Mike Vrabel's coaching debut with the Patriots. Smith is carrying that familiarity into his latest matchup.


              “They’ve got great players, they’re coached by Mike Vrabel, who’s a defensive guy, so we know he wants to have that defense be at the forefront and they want to establish the run as well on offense, so another great opportunity for us," Smith said.


              Smith's care of the football has allowed the Jets to enter with a plus-3 turnover differential, compared to a Patriots team that has forced a total of six turnovers, ranking 19th in the NFL entering Week 6.


              That's a concern for Vrabel.


              "(Smith has) done a fantastic job. And so, if you want to try to create turnovers, you’re going to have to actually go out and force them," Vrabel said.


              The Patriots also enter with a long list of players sustaining injuries, including left tackle Will Campbell (right knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle). That was on top of cornerback Christian Gonzalez missing his second straight game with a shoulder injury and Carlton Davis III sitting out with a neck injury.


              The good news is wide receiver A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time since going on injured reserve after sustaining a high ankle sprain in New England's season-opening loss at Seattle. He said he's impressed with how his fellow receivers performed in his absence.


              “Whenever I decide to come back, I'm just going to add,” Brown said.


              Need to know
              New York Jets (2-3) at New England (3-2)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS.


              Latest odds: Patriots by 7.


              Against the spread: Jets 3-1-1; Patriots 3-1-1.


              Last week: Jets beat Browns 17-12; Patriots beat Raiders 45-17.


              Last meeting: Patriots beat Jets 42-10 on Dec. 28, 2025, in East Rutherford, NJ.


              Series record: Patriots lead 77-56-1.


              Matchup to watch
              Patriots offensive line vs. Jets defensive line. The Jets have shown an ability to punch the ball out, recovering five fumbles so far. D

articles.headline: Arsenal's Eberechi Eze to perform Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired celebration after loss to IShowSpeed
articles.description: Eberechi Eze's next goal celebration has been determined by YouTuber IShowSpeed after the Arsenal forward was beaten by the influencer in an EA Sports FC battle.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルのエベレチ・エゼ、IShowSpeedに敗北しクリスティアーノ・ロナウド風のセレブレーションを披露することに
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナルのフォワード、エベレチ・エゼがEA Sports FCの対戦でインフルエンサーのIShowSpeedに敗れたため、次回のゴールセレブレーションが彼によって決定された。
articles.body:
Eberechi Eze's next goal celebration has been determined by YouTuber IShowSpeed after the Arsenal forward was beaten by the influencer in an EA Sports FC battle.

The best-of-three showdown was ultimately decided in favour of Speed, the 21-year-old streamer who has amassed 61.7 million subscribers on YouTube.

As a result, Eze will have to do a celebration of Speed's choosing -- a combination of Cristiano Ronaldo's trademark "siuuu" ritual and the streamer's signature bark, as well as a badge tap and a knee lift.

The Arsenal attacker chose Paris Saint-Germain for the opening match, with Speed questioning his decision not to choose Arsenal.

"I ride or die for my team, but on FIFA?" Eze replied. "I'm not sure about that."

Eze did play with his own team in the second game, before he lost to Speed who -- playing as Bayern Munich -- scored a dramatic late winner in the decider through ex-Tottenham man Harry Kane.

Speed initially suggested his own cross-arms celebration followed by twerking, a combination Eze rejected after laughing and saying: "I won't lie to you, that bounce thing is berserk."

He revealed he did not know how to backflip, which was option two, so the pair settled on the Ronaldo-inspired celebration.

articles.headline: Maxey: Healthy Embiid 'changes everything' for Sixers
articles.description: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.
articles.headlineJa: マクシー：「健康なエムビードがいれば、シックスターズのすべてが変わる」
articles.descriptionJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクシーは木曜日、ジョエル・エムビードが健康であることがシックスターズにとって「すべてを変える」と語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.

Embiid's 10-year career has been marred by injury. He has never played a full 82 games and has played more than 60 games just four times in his career. Over his 10 seasons, he has averaged just 49 games per season, which doesn't include him missing his first two seasons with injury.​

Embiid played just 38 games last season, double his number from 2024, as he navigated right hip complications, left knee management and appendicitis. The injuries have often kept Embiid out of training camp and the preseason -- crucial time for a team to get comfortable playing with a player like Embiid, the 2023 NBA MVP.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow."

Maxey said his experience gives him the advantage. He knows where Embiid likes to catch the ball, where he wants guards to cut and other tendencies that he has learned over six years of playing together. But many of the Sixers' new additions, most notably among them LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, don't have that luxury.

The difference this year is that they had a healthy Embiid in training camp and the preseason to make that transition easier.

​"If you haven't been playing with a big like Joel, there's not many. It's very hard, very difficult to learn certain things," he said. "...So, with him being here, we can drill those things over and over. It's been what, like two, three weeks that we've had just drilling and drilling. That's a good thing."

At the end of last season, Embiid said he was "as confident as I've ever been" about his health moving forward.

"I think, obviously, [my knee] was the biggest concern, and I'm not thinking about it," he said. "And as long as we keep doing what we've been doing, I won't have to think about it anymore.

articles.headline: 'Frustrated' Pierre Sage: Crystal Palace 'really far off' expectations in Lyon defeat
articles.description: Pierre Sage said Crystal Palace were "really far off" his expectations after suffering a 3-2 Europa League defeat away to his former side Lyon.
articles.headlineJa: 「苛立ちを感じている」ピエール・セージ：リヨンに敗れたクリスタル・パレスは期待から「大きくかけ離れている」
articles.descriptionJa: ピエール・セージは、かつての古巣リヨンとのヨーロッパリーグのアウェイ戦で3-2で敗れた後、クリスタル・パレスは自身の期待から「大きくかけ離れていた」と語った。
articles.body:
Pierre Sage said Crystal Palace were "really far off" his expectations after suffering a 3-2 Europa League defeat away to his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon's advantage late in a first half void of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino cut the deficit in half five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada's late goal proved a mere consolation.

"At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play," Sage said to PalaceTV.

"I think we didn't play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

"When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half."

Sage's side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that contest, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his side, but on Thursday night was left rueing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season's Conference League winners.

Sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month tenure with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner's, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

- Lyon 3-2 Crystal Palace: Visitors fall short in thriller against Sage's former club - as it happened

- Man United's Martínez issues apology for post-match outburst after meeting 

- Why does Haaland score so many goals? Because he's elite at staying onside

He told UEFA: "It's a very disappointing return because we lost. I can't take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn't there.

"The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

"We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

"I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool's Wirtz to Bayern Munich?
articles.description: Florian Wirtz could end up returning to the Bundesliga, as Bayern Munich are keeping a close eye on his situation at Liverpool. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂・ニュース：リヴァプールのヴィルツがバイエルン・ミュンヘンへ？
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルン・ミュンヘンがリヴァプールでの状況を注視しているため、フローリアン・ヴィルツがブンデスリーガに復帰する可能性がある。Transfer Talkが最新情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich could offer Florian Wirtz an escape route from the Premier League should he want to end his stay at Liverpool, while Lisandro Martínez's future at Manchester United is in question after his scathing critique of the club's board. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are keeping close tabs on the situation of Liverpool attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old hasn't reached the levels expected since making his move from Bayer Leverkusen to Anfield last summer, and there is a belief within the Allianz Arena that the Germany international would be open to a Bundesliga return. While the discussions within the German club are growing, they still remain exploratory rather than official.

- The future of Manchester United center back Lisandro Martínez has been called into question after his public criticism of the club's bosses, reports Sky Sports. The 28-year-old's contract expires in the summer, and there are real doubts about whether it will be renewed, especially as the Red Devils aim to revamp their defence as they look at new center backs and left backs. Martinez pushed for a move to Atlético Madrid in the summer, but no suitable offer came in for United to consider.

- AS Monaco's Folarin Balogun and Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth are the main names being looked at as Juventus aim to sign a striker, as reported by Tuttosport. Luciano Spalletti likes both strikers, and Balogun in particular is likely to make a transfer in January, as the 25-year-old's proposed summer move to Everton fell through due to a scandal involving his medical, and he has been left out of Monaco's Conference League squad. Jonathan David's loan from Juventus to Atleti could help open the door for Sorloth to go the other way.

- Liverpool have stepped up their pursuit of Tijuana attacking midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to TEAMtalk. Mora turned 18 years old yesterday, which removes any FIFA barrier to the Mexico international moving abroad and means a transfer could be possible in January. The Reds have followed up their earlier enquiries and are now strong contenders to sign Mora, who Tijuana want £30 million for, which would be a Liga MX record. Arsenal are also serious contenders, Borussia Dortmund and Benfica have previously held talks with Mora's representatives, while Real Madrid, Barcelona, Manchester City, Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain are also admirers.

- Arsenal, Atletico Madrid and Bayern Munich are all monitoring Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi, as reported by Nicolo Schira. The 22-year-old has previously received interest from Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur, but Brugge considered the Germany U21 international as non-transferrable. articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs dominate annual NBA GM survey
articles.description: An annual survey of NBA general managers projects the Spurs to win the NBA title this season, with Victor Wembanyama earning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year honors.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマとスパーズがNBA GM年次アンケートを席巻
articles.descriptionJa: NBAゼネラルマネージャーを対象とした年次アンケートで、今シーズンはスパーズがNBAタイトルを獲得し、ヴィクター・ウェンバンヤマがMVPと最優秀守備選手賞を受賞すると予想されている。
articles.body:
An annual survey of NBA general managers revealed Thursday that the league is bracing for a full takeover by Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs.

After winning 62 games and making a surprise trip to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs emerged as the survey's 2027 championship favorite, and Wembanyama was projected to win Most Valuable Player and be selected as the league's best defensive player.

In addition, the 7-foot-4 French center received 93% of the votes in response to the question: "If you were starting a franchise today and could sign any player in the NBA, who would it be?"

The general managers did not view the Spurs as overwhelming title favorites. San Antonio received 50% of the votes, narrowly topping the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder. The defending champion New York Knicks, who were picked to win the Eastern Conference, and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers, bolstered by LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, also received votes to win the title.

Wembanyama, 22, was selected as the heavy favorite to win his first MVP award with 77% of the votes. Denver's Nikola Jokic (10%) and Minnesota's Anthony Edwards (7%) also earned nods.

While Wembanyama was also selected as the "player who forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments," the "best international player" and "the most versatile player," he wasn't the only Spurs star to receive recognition in the extensive survey.

Dylan Harper, the 2025 No. 2 pick, was voted as the player most likely to enjoy a breakthrough season, topping Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg. Tobias Harris, a veteran forward who signed with San Antonio in free agency, was also named as the offseason's "most underrated player acquisition." Finally, the Spurs' young core, which includes Wembanyama, Harper and Stephon Castle, was named as the league's most promising.

The league's general managers deemed the 76ers as winners of the "best overall moves this offseason" for adding James and Brown, topping the Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets. However, Miami's trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo was viewed as the "acquisition who will make the biggest impact."

NBA.com has conducted a survey of the league's general managers for the past 25 seasons. This year's edition featured 48 questions regarding players, teams and recent transactions.

articles.headline: Man United's Martínez issues apology for post-match outburst after meeting
articles.description: Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマルティネス、会合後に試合後の激昂について謝罪
articles.descriptionJa: アトレティコ・マドリードに0-2で敗れた後、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの経営陣を批判したリサンドロ・マルティネスが、正式に謝罪した。
articles.body:
Lisandro Martínez has issued a formal apology after criticising Manchester United's board following Tuesday's 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina defender took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox during his post-match interviews and suggested head coach Michael Carrick has been let down by a lack of summer signings.

United's hierarchy, including Wilcox and Carrick, met with Martínez  at the club's training ground on Thursday before the 28-year-old released a statement apologising for his comments.

"Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager," Martínez said in a post on social media.

"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

"The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise."

United have chosen not to confirm whether Martínez has been disciplined for his outburst, although sources have told ESPN that he has been fined.

According to club sources, the matter is "considered closed" and Martínez is set to be available to face Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday if selected.

articles.headline: Las Vegas bettor Shane Hennen pleads guilty to charges related to fixing schemes
articles.description: A bettor indicted in three federal gambling cases pleaded guilty to charges related to schemes involving the NBA, NCAA and Chinese Basketball Association.
articles.body:
Shane Hennen, a Las Vegas sports bettor indicted in three high-profile federal gambling cases, pleaded guilty to charges related to betting schemes involving the NBA, the NCAA and the Chinese Basketball Association on Wednesday in Philadelphia.

Hennen pleaded guilty to sports bribery, aiding and abetting and conspiracy charges related to wire fraud and money laundering in two of the cases in federal court.

The maximum sentence is 125 years in prison, according to the Department of Justice's plea memorandum. His sentencing is scheduled for Feb. 25, 2027.

Federal prosecutors from the U.S. Attorney's Office in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania say Hennen participated in a nearly three-year scheme that began around September 2022 and aimed to fix basketball games in the Chinese Basketball Association CBA and in NCAA basketball.

"The defendant engaged in the scheme as a 'fixer,' working together with others who recruited and bribed CBA and NCAA men's basketball players to underperform and help ensure their team failed to cover the spread," federal prosecutors stated in the court documents. "The defendant then placed large wagers on those games, and arranged for others to do so, generating proceeds for the scheme."

Hennen also pleaded guilty to participating in a scheme to use nonpublic information to bet on NBA games and players in a case from the Eastern District of New York involving Terry Rozier.

An attorney for Hennen declined comment when reached Thursday by ESPN.

Hennen is still facing charges in a third case involving allegedly rigged poker games backed by the Mafia. NBA coach and Hall of Famer Chauncey Billups and former NBA player and coach Damon Jones were also indicted in the poker case.

articles.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
articles.description: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

articles.headline: Vinícius Júnior 'angry,' vows to return to top Real Madrid form
articles.description: Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior admits he is "angry" with himself and has vowed to return to top form.
articles.body:
Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior said he is "angry" with himself and has vowed to return to top form.

The Brazilian forward has set up three goals but scored just once in 10 appearances this season.

"I'm not saying I'm worried, but I'm angry with myself for not being in my best version," Vinícius told reporters after Madrid's 4-3 comeback win at Roma in Wednesday's Champions League game.

"In the end, Vini always returns. I am certain.

"It's a difficult time for me, but I have to keep working; things will turn around. I know I'm not at my best right now, but I've been through worse times before and managed to bounce back."

Vinícius, 26, in his ninth season at Madrid, agreed this summer a new deal to remain at the club until 2032.

"I arrived [at Madrid] very young, an 18-year-old, and I have always shown my face for this club, for this team," he said. "When I was 18, many people laughed at me, saying I wouldn't score any goals -- and today, I have over 100 with this jersey. Many titles, too... I don't even need to name them.

"Many have doubted me, yet I've always stood up for this club -- which is why I've signed on for another six years. But the good form will return, and the goals will come back; I'm certain of that -- I have no doubt at all."

It's been a difficult week for Vinícius. He was sent off in Madrid's 1-0 win over Villarreal on Saturday for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair.

Vinícius was handed a four-match ban which means he will miss the Clásico against Barcelona at the Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Although Vinícius started on Wednesday, he was visibly annoyed when he was replaced in the 59th minute with Madrid trailing 3-1. His Brazil teammate, Endrick, came on in his place and scored Madrid's equaliser after Carlos Espí had reduced the arrears.

- UCL talking points, MD2: Who's to blame for Man United mess? Chaos bad for Madrid?

- Mourinho takes blame for Madrid struggles before late rally stuns Roma

- Mourinho's subs spark Real Madrid comeback, but Champions League glory feels far away

"It's normal for me to get upset about being substituted because I always want to play, to be well to help the team," Vinícius said.

"Today it hasn't been possible. In the end, the substitutions helped us. They changed the match. Endrick came on and made a great impact -- he shifted the dynamic and even scored a goal. He was the best player in the second half. We hope he continues to develop so he can keep contributing, as should other players like Carlos [Espi], who often comes on for just a few minutes. They are really helping us a lot."

Vinícius will serve the first of his four-match ban on Sunday when Real Madrid host Sevilla in LaLiga.
